title: Flout at Your Own Risk: LLMs Struggle with Pragmatic Cooperativity Under Epistemic Asymmetry
abstract: arXiv:2607.11053v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Fruitful collaborations require effective communication of privately-held information. The increasing use of LLMs as "collaborators" raises questions about the extent to which they exhibit these pragmatic capabilities. In this paper, we perform a novel investigation into the pragmatic reasoning capabilities of LLMs in a multiparty collaborative task under partial information conditions. We first formalize a notion of collaborative epistemic asymmetry and prove that fully actionable instructions in this context requires adherence to Grice's cooperative principle. translated_title: 违反格赖斯准则风险自负：大语言模型在认知不对称下难以实现语用合作
translated_abstract: 富有成效的协作需要对私有信息的有效沟通。大语言模型（LLM）作为“协作者”的使用日益增多，这引发了关于它们在多大程度上具备这些语用能力的问题。在本文中，我们首次对大语言模型在部分信息条件下的多方协作任务中的语用推理能力进行了新颖的探究。我们首先形式化定义了“协作性认知不对称”这一概念，并证明在此情境下，完全可执行的指令必须遵循格赖斯合作原则。随后，我们实证评估了多种大语言模型作为说话者和倾听者进行合作的能力，涵盖提示工程与后训练等多种策略。结果表明，尽管大语言模型在协作环境中表现出一定的语用能力，但在信息不完整的语用沟通中仍然面临挑战，且格赖斯准则能够预测其不同的失败模式。
tldr: 本文形式化了“协作性认知不对称”概念并证明完全可执行的指令需遵循格赖斯合作原则，同时通过实证评估发现大语言模型在信息不完整的多方协作中无论作为说话者还是倾听者均存在语用沟通缺陷，且格赖斯准则可预测其不同失败模式。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes collaborative epistemic asymmetry, proves that fully actionable instructions require adherence to Grice's cooperative principle, and empirically shows that LLMs still struggle with pragmatic communication as both speakers and listeners under incomplete information in multiparty collaboration.
